# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 90 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 90 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_090_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 7

**1** "The fifth mountain with green grass and rugged terrain — these are those who believed and are faithful, but are difficult to please; they are presumptuous and self-opinionated, wanting to know everything but understanding nothing at all. **2** Because of their presumption, understanding has departed from them, and a certain rashness is mixed with their recklessness. These therefore are among the rocks of the mountain. **3** Yet God is not displeased with them, for they are good people with a certain hardness of character. If they restrain themselves and become truly meek, repentance is available to them. **4** "The sixth mountain with both large and small cracks — these are those who have believed: those in the small cracks quarrel among themselves and are weak in faith; those in the large cracks are presumptuous in wickedness and full of themselves. Repentance is open to these, but it is hard, and they shall live only with difficulty." **5** "The seventh mountain with green and cheerful grass on which cattle and all manner of animals fed, and birds also — these are those who believed and are innocent and guileless; they were never divided in heart, but always walked in joy. **6** "The eighth mountain full of springs from which all manner of creatures drank — these are the apostles and teachers who preached the name of the Son of God, and having fulfilled their charge, fell asleep in the power and holiness of the Son of God."

---

### Translator's Note
Mountain 5's portrait of the theologically presumptuous but essentially good — and mountain 7's innocent joy-walkers — form a pointed contrast. Mountain 8's apostles-as-springs is one of the most beautiful images in the Shepherd, depicting the apostolic generation as the source from which all subsequent Christian life flows. SOPHIA follows LOGOS throughout.
